questions: Q1: Is the core phenomenon reproducible in principle (independent replication feasible)?
Q2: Are the measurements, statistics, and data analysis sound and appropriately controlled?
Q3: Are the theoretical claims supported by the evidence presented (no overreach)?
Q4: Were alternative explanations adequately considered and ruled out?

results.title: Framework-templated gas lattices in metal-organic frameworks

q1.note: GCMC simulations reproducible; Co-CAU-36 synthesis feasible though not yet experimentally confirmed.

q2.note: Large-scale screening + ML inverse design with clear stats. GCMC is standard.

q3.note: Claims limited to computational prediction; no experimental overreach.

q4.note: Other MOFs screened; inverse design tests designability vs incidental occurrence.

results.title: Visualization of the Zhang-Rice singlet, electronic molecules and Cooper pair formation in a cuprate superconductor

q1.note: STM/STS on CCOC reproducible by other UHV-STM groups.

q2.note: Large-area atomic-scale imaging across doping series. Systematic Na substitution control.

q3.note: Direct visualization claim conservative; 'electronic molecules' is descriptive model.

q4.note: Explicit comparison against undoped parent and superconducting samples.

results.title: GDF15 suppresses liver inflammation independently of weight loss through neuroendocrine glucocorticoid signaling

q1.note: Mouse MASH models standard; GDF15 commercially available.

q2.note: Genetic, pharmacological, genomic, spatial transcriptomics. Multiple orthogonal methods.

q3.note: 'Independently of weight loss' explicitly tested and supported.

q4.note: Distinguished from prior 2023 GDF15 calorie-burning study.

results.title: BlackTHUNDER: Evidence of three massive black holes in a z ~ 5 galaxy

q1.note: JWST NIRSpec-IFS data public; spectro-astrometry standard and reproducible.

q2.note: Spatially resolved spectroscopy with independent spatial shifts. Two-year baseline.

q3.note: Mass estimates have acknowledged uncertainties; Eddington exceedance noted as expected.

q4.note: Tested single-BH-with-unusual-gas, outflows, SNe, winds, shocks. All disfavored.

results.title: NASA Dragonfly flight fuselage integration begins for Titan exploration

q1.note: Engineering milestone verifiable by NASA documentation.

q2.note: Ground-vibration, pressure-leak, and wind-tunnel testing standard.

q3.note: 40x efficiency labeled as ideal theory comparison, not measured flight.

q4.note: Acknowledges real flight harder: coaxial wakes, drag, motor losses, winds.

results.title: Physicists are closing in on the origin of matter via baryon number transport

q1.note: RHIC/STAR data archived; isobaric analysis reproducible.

q2.note: Same proton+neutron total, different proton count provides clean tag.

q3.note: Framed as 'new clue', not solution to asymmetry.

q4.note: Addresses prior quark-only assumption; gluon role is the tested alternative.

results.title: Astronomers discover a black hole 'star' (MoM-BH*-1) at cosmic dawn

q1.note: JWST spectroscopy reproducible; object in public archives.

q2.note: Strongest Balmer break quantified; compared against stellar and dust models.

q3.note: Model presented as interpretation; 'could belong to' LRDs is cautious.

q4.note: Dust-obscured AGN, normal stars, new stellar atmospheres all considered.

results.title: Magnonic spontaneous oscillation induced by parametric pumping

q1.note: YIG waveguide + parametric pumping reproducible in magnonics labs.

q2.note: Linewidth, Q-factor, phase-locking quantified. Frequency tuning demonstrated.

q3.note: 'Controllable platform' and 'pathway toward' — appropriately scoped.

q4.note: Contrasts with prior three-wave and four-wave mixing limits.

results.title: Remnants of Theia discovered as large low-velocity provinces deep in Earth's mantle

q1.note: Seismic data archived; simulations reproducible with standard codes.

q2.note: Hydrodynamic + thermal + convection simulations combined.

q3.note: Presented as hypothesis ('may contain'), not fact.

q4.note: Subducted crust and magma ocean alternatives discussed. Chemical tests proposed.

results.title: No cosmological constraints on dark photon dark matter from resonant conversion

q1.note: Plasma physics simulations reproducible; standard equations.

q2.note: Nonlinear simulations contrasted with 15-year linear treatment.

q3.note: Negative claim ('no cosmological constraints') is conservative.

q4.note: Linear treatment explicitly tested and shown to fail.

results.title: Andromeda's star formation has declined sharply over past 500 million years

q1.note: Hubble PHAT+PHAST public; color-magnitude analysis standard.

q2.note: ~200M stars across thousands of cells. Color-age mapping standard.

q3.note: M32 connection is 'most likely suspect' with 3D position uncertainty noted.

q4.note: Internal settling and gas consumption considered; M32 causation not claimed proven.

results.title: Bound states in the continuum of gravitational waves

q1.note: Metric perturbation calculations mathematically reproducible.

q2.note: Analytical derivation with clear assumptions. Conservation checked.

q3.note: Explicitly theoretical. 'Could' and 'may' throughout.

q4.note: Acknowledges theoretical proposal. Quasi-BICs noted as next challenge.

results.title: Planet formation at cosmic dawn: planetesimals in H2O-rich disks around low-mass stars

q1.note: Cosmological simulation chain reproducible with standard codes.

q2.note: Pop III SN -> enrichment -> disk -> solids chain presented.

q3.note: 'Could potentially' and 'may have existed' — cautious.

q4.note: Acknowledges prior slow-formation assumption; positions as counter-evidence.

results.title: Initial demonstration of a quantum heat engine based on dissipation-engineered superconducting circuits

q1.note: Superconducting circuit experiments reproducible in similar cryo facilities.

q2.note: Otto cycle with timed pulses. Qubit state monitored. Positive work quantified.

q3.note: 'Initial demonstration' and 'could contribute' — scoped.

q4.note: Distinguished from prior non-cyclic/non-superconducting engines.

results.title: Twenty-year blazar monitoring of PKS 2155-304 reveals hadronic neutrino signatures

q1.note: Swift and Fermi data public. 20-year lightcurve reproducible.

q2.note: Long baseline reduces flukes. Two-telescope cross-calibration.

q3.note: Hadronic origin 'most likely' per theory; neutrino link suggestive.

q4.note: Single-population electron models tested and rejected.

results.title: Two independent studies push semiconductor qubits towards practical scales

q1.note: Both devices reproducible in semiconductor fab facilities.

q2.note: Two independent Nature studies. 5-qubit entanglement and 10x improvement quantified.

q3.note: 'Paving the way' — cautious about full-scale timeline.

q4.note: Complementary approaches acknowledged. Both note remaining distance to scale.

results.title: Venus may have hidden vast oceans for billions of years

q1.note: Magellan data archived; morphological analysis reproducible.

q2.note: Tesserae compared to Earth analogues at same scale. Global mapping.

q3.note: 'Compelling case' and 'may have' — cautious. 90% is model output.

q4.note: 'Not unambiguous' stated. Dry volcanic model acknowledged. Future missions proposed.

results.title: Initial mass function varies with star-forming environment

q1.note: Gaia DR3 public. Cluster analysis reproducible.

q2.note: Nearly 2 billion stars mapped. Cluster sample provides control.

q3.note: Does not discard IMF; proposes environment-dependent refinement.

q4.note: Does not claim to explain all JWST massive galaxies; one possible factor.

results.title: Chemical fingerprints of binary mass transfer in massive stars

q1.note: MESA inputs on Zenodo. Spectroscopic abundances standard.

q2.note: Comprehensive binary grid. Analytic framework independent of specific models.

q3.note: Gamma Columbae reclassification evidence-based; uncertainties acknowledged.

q4.note: Distinguishes gainers from donors, rotating single stars, and mergers.

results.title: IBM quantum computing models tritium behavior in fusion reactor blankets

q1.note: IBM quantum hardware limited but computation reproducible on similar devices.

q2.note: Nine configurations tested; hybrid quantum-classical is standard NISQ approach.

q3.note: 'First-known instance' accurate for this application. Concrete output.

q4.note: No classical benchmark (DFT/CCSD(T)) presented in news report for this FLiBe system.

results.title: Full sound rainbows created and imaged for the first time

q1.note: Elastic wave devices reproducible in phononics labs.

q2.note: Two independent teams strengthens reproducibility.

q3.note: 'Could lead to' — appropriately speculative.

q4.note: News report lacks detail on prior theoretical predictions and alternative frequency-sorting mechanisms.

results.title: Physicists extend Hawking's black hole laws to dynamical objects

q1.note: Mathematical derivation from Einstein equations fully reproducible.

q2.note: Dynamical horizons used in numerical relativity for decades.

q3.note: Extends Hawking-Bekenstein without overturning. Mathematically derived.

q4.note: Addresses 1990s teleology problem. Prior Ashtekar work acknowledged.
